title: louiselm.nvim: pure ACP client for Neovim — v1 core + phased roadmap
description:
## Problem Statement

As a daily Neovim + agent user, my current plugin (codecompanion.nvim) fights my workflow in three ways. First, config mistakes fail silently: a mistyped key is absorbed by deep-merge and the feature it configures is skipped without a word. Second, its architecture is a general adapter abstraction normalizing HTTP providers and ACP into one interface, while I use exclusively ACP agents (claude-agent-acp, codex-acp, acp-llm-adapter, copilot ACP) — I pay the complexity of a layer I do not use. Third, it gives me no path to the feature I actually want next: a swarm of agents collaboratively working a queue of beads tasks. My core workflow — grill an idea in chat, converge on a plan, convert the plan into beads via skills — must keep working, uniformly, across all my agents.

## Solution

louiselm.nvim: a pure ACP client for Neovim. Agents are external processes declared in config; anything non-ACP reaches the plugin through external bridges (acp-llm-adapter, opencode acp), never through in-plugin providers. The core is built swarm-ready from day one: a multi-session registry with a headless Lua API, typed events, pluggable permission policies, and addressable sessions — so the future orchestrator is an additional consumer of the public API, not a rewrite. Configuration is validated militantly against a single declarative schema that also generates the LuaCATS types and the documentation. Skills are discovered from a central repo and made available to every agent via a thin index-injection mechanism with a per-agent native/inject/off policy.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to declare each agent (command, args, env, options) in my config, so that adding a backend is a config entry, never plugin code.
2. As a user, I want any unknown config key to produce a hard error with a fuzzy "did you mean" suggestion, so that typos can never silently disable a feature.
3. As a user, I want wrong types or invalid values to error with the expected type, the received value, and a valid example, so that I can fix mistakes without reading source.
4. As a user, I want all config errors collected and reported in one structured report, so that I fix everything in a single pass instead of a fix-reload loop.
5. As a user, I want the plugin to refuse to start on invalid config, so that I am never unknowingly running on silently substituted defaults.
6. As a user, I want deprecated keys to warn with a migration path, so that upgrades guide me instead of breaking me.
7. As a user, I want editor completion and type checking while writing my config, so that most mistakes are caught before the validator ever runs.
8. As a user, I want :checkhealth to re-run validation plus environment checks (agent binaries on PATH, versions, skill paths exist), so that a broken setup is diagnosable in one command.
9. As a user, I want a chat buffer with streamed markdown and a visible tool-call timeline, so that I can follow what the agent is doing while it does it.
10. As a user, I want to pick which agent a new session uses and switch between concurrent sessions, so that several conversations can live side by side.
11. As a user, I want agent-requested file edits and commands gated by a permission flow, so that nothing touches my system without policy saying so.
12. As a user, I want agent file edits reviewable as diffs, so that I can inspect changes before or after approving them.
13. As a user, I want permissions evaluated by pluggable policy objects with "ask the human" merely the default, so that future autonomous sessions can run scoped auto-approval policies without core changes.
14. As a user, I want to mention the current buffer, send a visual selection, and fuzzy-pick files into the conversation, so that pointing the agent at context is one gesture.
15. As a user, I want slash commands advertised by the agent over ACP to appear in the chat's command menu, so that agent capabilities surface without client-side duplication.
16. As a user, I want skills discovered from my central skill repo (~/.config/agentskills, Agent Skills / SKILL.md format), so that one skill tree serves every agent.
17. As a user, I want a per-agent skills policy (native, inject, off) with inject sending only a skill index that the agent expands by reading files itself, so that skills work on skill-less agents without heavy client machinery.
18. As a user, I want symlink-aware overlap detection between an agent's native skill dir and my configured skill paths, so that a skill is never loaded twice into one context.
19. As a user, I want a skill invocation picker in chat, so that starting a grill-me session is a keystroke, on any agent.
20. As a user, I want my grill-me → plan → beads workflow to run purely through skills and the agent executing the beads CLI itself, so that the plugin core stays tracker-ignorant.
21. As a plugin consumer (or future orchestrator), I want a headless Lua API — create session against a named agent, prompt, receive streamed updates via callbacks, cancel, dispose — so that everything the UI does is scriptable without UI.
22. As a plugin consumer, I want typed events emitted for every session lifecycle moment (chunk, tool call started/finished, permission requested, turn done, error), so that dashboards and orchestrators can subscribe without patching internals.
23. As a user, I want every session addressable by id with inspectable state (agent, status, working dir, current turn), so that a future swarm dashboard has substrate to read.
24. As a user, I want a crashed or misbehaving agent process to surface as a loud, specific session error — never a hang or a silent death — so that failure modes are as strict as config validation.
25. As a contributor, I want the ACP layer conformance-tested against a mock agent in CI, so that protocol correctness is verified without real LLMs or API keys.

## Implementation Decisions

- Pure ACP client, hard boundary: no in-plugin HTTP providers ever; non-ACP backends go through external bridges. Internally one small agent interface with ACP as its sole implementation, preserving the seam for a hypothetical future transport.
- Five hard architectural constraints checked against every PR: (1) multi-session registry, no singleton chat; (2) headless API with the UI as its first consumer; (3) typed event system; (4) permission policies as pluggable objects, human prompt as default policy; (5) sessions addressable, listable, inspectable.
- Modules: schema (config DSL, validator, error reporter; single source generating LuaCATS types and vimdoc), acp (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio via vim.system pipes, typed against the protocol schema), session (registry, headless API, events, process lifecycle), permission (policy engine), skills (discovery, index injection, per-agent policy, overlap detection), ui.chat, ui.diff, health, and a dev-only mock ACP agent.
- Config validation is militant: unknown key or wrong type is a hard error; errors are collected exhaustively then reported; plugin refuses to start on any error; deprecated keys warn with migration path.
- Skills: hybrid thin design. Discovery from configured paths; injection sends only name/description/path and relies on the agent's own file tools for progressive disclosure; native|inject|off per agent (native default for agents with native skill support); full-content injection fallback for tool-less agents is a later refinement.
- Chat context is deliberately thin: buffer mention, visual selection, file picker, agent slash-command passthrough, skill picker. Agents explore the project themselves; the client points.
- Tech foundation: Neovim floor = latest stable at release, moving forward aggressively; zero runtime dependencies (no plenary, no nui); picker integrations explicitly configured and validated, never silently auto-detected; LuaCATS everywhere with lua-language-server as a CI gate.
- Phasing: P0 foundation (schema, acp, session, agent defs) → P1 daily driver (chat, permissions, diff, context, skills; exit criterion: codecompanion uninstalled, grill-me → beads works on all four agents) → P2 comfort (inline assistant on the same session core, history via ACP session/load, full-content skill fallback, multi-session UX) → P3 swarm (opens with its own grill-me).
- Rust is welcome where it earns its place: the swarm orchestrator binary is the named candidate (long-running external process, async runtime, same ecosystem as beads_rust); the core editor-side client stays pure Lua.

## Testing Decisions

- mini.test as the sole, dev-only test dependency.
- schema, acp, session, permission, and skills get full headless unit coverage; the headless API constraint exists partly to make this trivial.
- acp and session additionally get integration coverage driving the mock ACP agent end to end (spawn, initialize, session, prompt, streamed updates, permission round-trip, cancel, agent-crash surfacing).
- A good test here exercises a module through its public interface only; the five architectural constraints are themselves enforced by tests (e.g. two concurrent sessions prompting simultaneously is a required passing case from P0).
- UI modules get smoke tests via child Neovim processes; no pixel-level assertions.
- Validator tests include the adversarial cases: typo'd keys at every nesting depth, wrong types, valid-looking-but-unknown sections, and the symlink-overlap skill scenario.

## Out of Scope

- Completion / ghost text: dropped permanently; other plugins own that space.
- In-plugin HTTP or provider adapters of any kind.
- A prompt library separate from skills.
- The swarm orchestrator's design (in-nvim vs external Rust binary, scheduling, worktree isolation): deferred to a dedicated grill-me that opens Phase 3. This epic only guarantees its prerequisites.
- Beads-specific core code; the optional beads dashboard/picker is a future extension on the public API.
- RAG, indexing, web search: agent-side concerns.

## Further Notes

- Ecosystem bet acknowledged: louiselm wagers on ACP's continued adoption (Zed-originated; gemini-cli, opencode, goose, amp, claude, codex all speak it). The internal agent interface is the hedge.
- Risk: ACP spec evolution (e.g. session/load, command advertisement) may shift; the protocol layer should pin a spec version and negotiate capabilities explicitly.
- The user's central skill repo pattern (~/.config/agentskills with per-agent symlinks) is the reference deployment; overlap detection must resolve symlinks before comparing paths.
- Follow-up work items after this epic lands: per-phase decomposition via to-beads-feature / to-beads-tasks, starting with P0.

title: P0: Config schema DSL + militant validator
description:
## Scope
Single-source declarative config schema that generates LuaCATS types, vimdoc, and drives runtime validation. Militant: unknown keys are hard errors with fuzzy "did you mean"; wrong types error with expected/received/example; all errors collected and reported in one pass; plugin refuses to start on any error; deprecated keys warn with migration path.

## User stories covered
2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

## Modules
- `lua/louiselm/schema/init.lua` — schema DSL (describe key shape, type, default, validator fns)
- `lua/louiselm/schema/validate.lua` — recursive validator, error collector
- `lua/louiselm/schema/report.lua` — structured error report formatter
- `lua/louiselm/schema/gen_luacats.lua` — emit LuaCATS annotations from schema
- `lua/louiselm/schema/gen_vimdoc.lua` — emit vimdoc from schema

## Acceptance criteria
- Unknown key at any nesting depth → hard error with fuzzy suggestion
- Wrong type → error with expected type, received value, valid example
- All errors surface in one structured report (no fix-reload loop)
- Plugin setup() returns false on any validation error
- Deprecated key → warning with migration path, plugin still starts
- LuaCATS output passes lua-language-server CI gate
- Generated vimdoc matches schema structure
- mini.test coverage for adversarial cases: typo at depth, wrong types, valid-looking unknown sections
close_reason: Completed schema DSL, exhaustive validation, structured reporting, setup gating, deprecation warnings, LuaCATS generation, and vimdoc generation. Added recursive vimdoc coverage for array-of table fields; all 18 MiniTest cases, stylua, LuaLS, and generated LuaCATS validation pass.

Modules: lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua, protocol.lua, transport.lua.

title: P0: Permission policy engine
description: Pluggable policy objects with human-prompt as default. Gate file edits and commands. Policies: ask-human (default), auto-approve-scoped (for future autonomous sessions). Diff review integration point. Covers user stories 11, 12, 13. Modules: lua/louiselm/permission/init.lua, policy.lua, gates.lua, human-prompt.lua.
close_reason: Implemented permission policies and ACP gates: ask-human default, scoped auto-approval for file paths and command argv, normalized path checks, automatic ACP allow/cancel responses, session policy integration, public API/docs, and tests. Verified 55 MiniTest cases, StyLua, and LuaLS.

title: T: Schema DSL core — describe API for key shapes, types, defaults, validators
description:
Implement the schema description DSL in lua/louiselm/schema/init.lua. API: `Schema.define(spec)` that accepts nested key descriptions with type, default, description, and optional validator functions. Must support: string, number, boolean, table (nested), array-of, one-of types. Output is a normalized schema table consumed by the validator and generators.

Files: lua/louiselm/schema/init.lua (+ tests in tests/schema/dsl_spec.lua)
AC: mini.test coverage for all supported types, nested schemas, and validator attachment.
close_reason: Implemented normalized Schema.define DSL for primitive, nested table, array-of, and one-of types with defaults, descriptions, validators, dense-sequence checks, and explicit errors. Added MiniTest coverage and test init. Verified stylua, lua-language-server, and direct headless API smoke; MiniTest execution is unavailable because mini.test is not installed.

title: T: Recursive validator — walk config tree, collect all errors exhaustively
description:
Implement recursive validator in lua/louiselm/schema/validate.lua. Walks user config against normalized schema. Collects ALL errors (never short-circuits on first error). Error types: unknown_key (with fuzzy "did you mean" via string distance), wrong_type (expected X, got Y, example Z), missing_required, validation_failed (custom validator returned false).

Files: lua/louiselm/schema/validate.lua (+ tests in tests/schema/validate_spec.lua)
AC: Adversarial test cases — typo at depth 3, wrong type at root, valid-looking unknown section, multiple simultaneous errors all reported.
close_reason: Implemented exhaustive recursive validation with unknown-key suggestions, type/example errors, required-field checks, custom validators, nested arrays, one-of values, and 5 adversarial MiniTest cases.

title: T: Error reporter — structured format with fuzzy suggestions and examples
description:
Implement structured error reporter in lua/louiselm/schema/report.lua. Takes the error list from the validator and formats a human-readable report. Each error includes: key path (e.g. "agents.claude.model"), error type, message, and where applicable: fuzzy suggestion, expected type, received value, valid example. Report is returned as a table consumable by both :checkhealth and startup error messages.

Files: lua/louiselm/schema/report.lua (+ tests in tests/schema/report_spec.lua)
AC: Report for 5 simultaneous errors is well-formatted. Fuzzy suggestions are correct for Levenshtein distance ≤ 3.
close_reason: Implemented structured validation reports with preserved error fields, human-readable messages, aggregate text and lines, fuzzy suggestions, expected types, examples, and 2 MiniTest cases.

title: T: LuaCATS generator — emit annotations from schema for editor completion
description:
Implement LuaCATS annotation generator in lua/louiselm/schema/gen_luacats.lua. Walks the normalized schema and emits ---@class, ---@field, ---@type annotations so that lua-language-server provides completion and type-checking while users write their config. Output must be a valid LuaCATS file that passes lua-language-server CI gate.

Files: lua/louiselm/schema/gen_luacats.lua (+ tests in tests/schema/gen_luacats_spec.lua)
AC: Generated file passes lua-language-server --check with zero diagnostics. All schema fields have corresponding annotations.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic LuaCATS generation for normalized schemas with nested classes, optional defaulted fields, arrays, unions, descriptions, and 2 MiniTest cases.

title: T: Vimdoc generator — emit help docs from schema
description:
Implement vimdoc generator in lua/louiselm/schema/gen_vimdoc.lua. Walks the normalized schema and emits Neovim help file format (*louiselm.txt*). Documents every config key with type, default, description. Must be a valid vimdoc file viewable with :help louiselm.

Files: lua/louiselm/schema/gen_vimdoc.lua (+ tests in tests/schema/gen_vimdoc_spec.lua)
AC: Generated file opens with :help louiselm and displays all config keys. Format is standard vimdoc (tags, sections, proper line wrapping).
close_reason: Implemented deterministic Neovim help generation with standard tags, configuration sections, nested key tags, defaults, descriptions, deprecation notes, and wrapped text; added 2 MiniTest cases.

title: T: Setup gate — refuse plugin start on invalid config, deprecation warnings
description:
Wire the schema system into plugin setup() in lua/louiselm/init.lua. On setup(): run validation, if errors exist return false and display the structured error report. Deprecated keys: warn with migration path but allow startup. Add deprecation tracking to schema DSL (Schema.deprecated(key, { message, migration })).

Files: lua/louiselm/init.lua (modify), lua/louiselm/schema/deprecate.lua (+ tests)
AC: Invalid config → setup() returns false, user sees full error report. Valid config → plugin starts normally. Deprecated key → warning + migration path, plugin starts. All 3 cases covered by mini.test.
close_reason: Implemented explicit-schema setup gating with full validation reports, user-facing invalid-config errors, immutable Schema.deprecated metadata, nested deprecation discovery, migration warnings, and 3 MiniTest cases.

title: Rewrite AGENTS.md for strict idiomatic Neovim Lua
description:
## Goal
Replace the inherited Rust policy with a compact, strict, idiomatic Neovim Lua engineering contract focused on correctness, clarity, simplicity, and fast delivery.

## Scope
- In scope: rewrite the existing AGENTS.md in place for louiselm.nvim; target Neovim embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1; define StyLua, lua-language-server, and mini.test gates; lightweight red-green-refactor; LuaCATS/public API rules; module/state/table ownership; structured errors and UI boundaries; strict config validation; safe async vim.system usage; zero runtime dependencies; Neovim API preferences; dangerous Lua escape hatches; concise editing and completion discipline.
- Out of scope: adding formatter, language-server, test harness, Makefile, or CI files; implementing plugin code; including Beads/bv workflow documentation; generic standalone Lua 5.2-5.4 compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. AGENTS.md contains no Rust/Cargo/Clippy/unsafe-specific policy and no Beads workflow section.
2. The policy is concise and project-specific, with current-stable Neovim and embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1 as its runtime contract.
3. The document captures every agreed quality, architecture, error-handling, validation, async/process, dependency, testing, typing, and editing rule without speculative frameworks or compatibility shims.
4. TDD is mandatory for meaningful behavior changes but explicitly lightweight and delivery-oriented.
5. Formatting/static/test completion gates are explicit, and unavailable gates must be reported rather than claimed passing.

## Testing
- Review the rendered Markdown structure and run a text search proving Rust and Beads-specific instructions are gone.
- Check the diff for whitespace errors.
- No Lua project gates are runnable yet because this task intentionally adds no Lua/tooling files.

## Notes
- Rewrite the existing file only; do not proliferate files.
- Prefer enforceable rules over explanatory handbook material.
close_reason: Replaced the inherited Rust policy with a compact strict Neovim Lua contract. Verified no Rust or Beads terms remain; tracked and untracked whitespace checks produced no errors. Lua quality gates are not applicable yet because the repository has no Lua files, LuaLS config, or MiniTest harness.

title: T: Install and integrate mini.test test dependency
description:
Make the headless MiniTest suite runnable in local development and CI.

Implementation guidance:
- Treat mini.test as a dev-only dependency; do not add runtime Lua dependencies or vendor source into lua/.
- Install a pinned mini.nvim revision (mini.test is provided by mini.nvim) into an ignored .deps/ checkout through a small idempotent setup entrypoint, or use an equivalent reproducible CI cache/install mechanism.
- Wire the installed checkout into tests/minimal_init.lua before requiring mini.test, with a clear failure when the dependency is missing.
- Keep the repository quality command runnable: nvim --headless --noplugin -u ./tests/minimal_init.lua -c "lua MiniTest.run()" -c "qa!".
- Document the install command and the pinned revision; CI should install/cache the same revision and execute the full MiniTest suite.

Acceptance criteria:
- A fresh checkout can install the pinned mini.test dependency with one documented command.
- The existing schema DSL tests run and pass through MiniTest.
- The exact repository test command runs successfully in a dependency-present environment.
- Missing dependency errors are specific and actionable.
- stylua and lua-language-server remain clean, and no runtime dependency or package-path mutation is introduced outside the test harness.
close_reason: Integrated mini.test as a dev-only dependency. Added pinned mini.nvim v0.18.0 checkout installer at scripts/install-test-deps, ignored .deps/, documented setup and test commands, and wired tests/minimal_init.lua with explicit *_spec.lua discovery and actionable missing-dependency errors. Verified repeated installation, exact MiniTest command (3/3 passing), StyLua, LuaLS, shell syntax, and dependency path handling.

title: Chat UI buffer updates run in fast event context
description: Running :LouiselmChat and receiving ACP process output raises E5560 because lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua calls nvim_buf_is_valid and other buffer APIs directly from the fast-event stdout callback. Marshal session event handling to the main loop while preserving event order and ignoring disposed views.
close_reason: Marshal chat session events with nvim.schedule before buffer access; added regression coverage. StyLua, lua-language-server, and all 43 mini.test cases pass.

title: Strengthen async UI testing contract
description: Follow-up to louiselm-8qk. Clarify that vim.system/RPC/stdout/libuv callbacks are fast-event callbacks, require an explicit scheduling boundary before editor/UI APIs, and require tests to model production callback context plus late results after dispose.
close_reason: Clarified fast-event callback rules, explicit vim.schedule UI boundaries, context-faithful async tests, and late-after-dispose coverage requirements in AGENTS.md. Verified git diff check, StyLua, LuaLS, and all 43 mini.test cases.

title: OOB chat startup fails in minimal and manual init
description: Reproduction A: from the repository root run nvim -u tests/minimal_init.lua, then execute :LouiselmChat (the reported spelling was :LouisLMChat). The chat buffer opens as '# default · session-1' but shows 'Error: ACP session/new failed: Invalid params' and an empty prompt. Expected: the documented minimal init provides a working out-of-the-box chat session with the default agent, or reports a specific actionable setup error. Reproduction B: run nvim -u manual_init.lua, update packages, then execute :LouiselmChat (the reported spelling also included :LuiseLmChat). Observed: E492 not an editor command: Lou..., so the command is unavailable after the package bootstrap. Expected: manual_init.lua exposes the same documented chat command, or clearly documents the required setup step. Acceptance criteria: reproduce both paths, fix the ACP session/new parameter mismatch, register the chat command in the manual bootstrap, verify the exact canonical command spelling, and add headless regression coverage for both startup paths.

title: Explain the LouiseLM vision and recursive identity
description:
## Problem Statement

The README documents development and implemented APIs but does not explain why LouiseLM exists, what the name means, or how its current ACP-backed Neovim foundation relates to the larger idea-to-software vision. Readers cannot yet understand the project before reaching the technical reference.

## Solution

Add a clear product narrative and an original hero banner at the start of the README. Present LouiseLM as alpha software whose north star is turning ideas into software, explain the attention-preserving workflow and its safety boundaries, and show the current manual workflow as one replaceable configuration. Preserve the existing technical reference beneath a concise bridge describing what works today.

## User Stories

1. As a new reader, I want to understand LouiseLM and its recursive name immediately, so that I can decide whether the project matters to me.
2. As a potential user, I want the vision separated clearly from current alpha capabilities, so that I am inspired without being misled.
3. As a creative developer, I want to see a strong default workflow presented as configurable, so that I can imagine building a different workflow with the same substrate.
4. As an operator, I want the vision to preserve my attention, ownership, and approval authority, so that automation remains empowering and legible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The README uses LouiseLM as the project name and includes the exact recursive acronym: LouiseLM Organizes Unruled Intelligent Systems into Emancipated Language Meshes.
2. The opening states that LouiseLM turns ideas into software and clearly labels the project as alpha software.
3. The motivation explains that ideas arrive faster than sustained attention and uses the gardening example without clinical or medical positioning.
4. The vision covers interruption-free capture, later enrichment and explainable triage, focused deliberation, planning, dependency-shaped execution, agent implementation and review, human approval, and an observable operator control plane.
5. Neovim is presented as the deliberate home and cockpit, with headless automation and optional future capture surfaces rather than a promised editor-independent runtime.
6. Local-first ownership, configurable workflow boundaries, strong defaults, replaceable parts, and policy-controlled automation are explicit principles.
7. The current grill-me to plan to beads to coding-agent flow appears as one possible configuration; grill-me, beads, bv, bvr, particular models, and CodeCompanion are not presented as LouiseLM requirements. CodeCompanion is not mentioned.
8. Current ACP chat and session capabilities are distinguished from unimplemented idea capture, ranking, orchestration, and dashboard work.
9. An original banner depicts Louise Michel within a decentralized mesh of people, agents, models, skills, tools, voice capture, ideas, and code. It uses a red, black, and white Commune-era printmaking aesthetic fused with a modern systems diagram, informed by Metelkova street-art energy, with no labels or explanatory text.
10. Existing technical instructions remain accurate and mostly intact beneath the new narrative.

## Implementation Notes

- Expand the top of the existing README rather than replacing the technical reference.
- Add one project-local raster hero asset and reference it with a repository-relative path.
- Use project voice: one brief empowering manifesto-like passage followed by concrete language.
- The visual carries the Louise Michel reference; do not explain that reference in prose.
- Emancipation concerns ideas, workflows, and user choice, never unbounded agent authority.

## Testing Notes

- Documentation and image generation do not require an artificial red test.
- Inspect the final Markdown structure and rendered image reference.
- Run formatting, static-analysis, test, and diff checks required by the repository contract; report any unavailable gate.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing idea storage, capture devices, voice transcription, scheduling, triage, orchestration, dashboards, or agent review.
- Designing a formal plugin API, workflow event schema, storage architecture, mobile application, external daemon, graph UI, or swarm scheduler.
- Changing existing public Lua APIs or technical behavior.
close_reason: Expanded README with the agreed LouiseLM vision, recursive acronym, alpha/current-state boundary, configurable workflow example, attention and safety principles, and corrected single-file test command. Added and inspected an original 1774x887 red-black-white mesh hero as a 640 KB WebP. Verification: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems; all 66 MiniTest cases passed after rerunning outside the read-only temp-file sandbox; git diff --check passed; external essay link returned HTTP 200.

title: Future vision: attention-preserving idea-to-software workflow
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas can arrive faster than sustained attention can evaluate them. A focused LouiseLM conversation should not be derailed by a new thought, yet the thought must not be lost. Over time, ideas also need a path from raw capture through deliberation and planning to software implementation, with the human spending attention on judgment and agents handling more routine throughput.

## Solution

Design and incrementally build an attention-preserving idea-to-software workflow for LouiseLM. Capture raw ideas locally without interrupting active work, enrich and rank them with explainable recommendations, resurface them at configurable workflow boundaries, and move approved ideas through deliberation, dependency-shaped planning, and policy-controlled agent execution.

The epic must include an example LouiseLM configuration that demonstrates one real workflow without making it a hard-coded product requirement:

grill-me conversation → agreed plan → to-beads decomposition → br/bv/bvr graph triage → phase-appropriate coding agents.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to capture a side thought in seconds while a focused chat continues unchanged, so that new ideas do not disappear or steal my current attention.
2. As a user, I want the original idea preserved exactly while agents add metadata and relationships, so that enrichment never silently rewrites my memory.
3. As a user, I want ideas resurfaced at the end of a focused session by default, with configurable workflow boundaries, so that interruptions remain under my control.
4. As a user, I want recommendations to explain why an idea was selected, so that ranking is inspectable rather than a black box.
5. As a user, I want policies to decide whether a recommendation is shown, queued, grilled, or advanced, so that safe automation can grow without removing approval gates.
6. As a user, I want stronger models available for deliberation and cheaper or faster agents available for well-specified implementation, so that attention and cost match the phase of work.
7. As a user, I want a Neovim control plane that makes ideas, projects, agent activity, blockers, progress, and human-attention points visible, so that automation remains understandable.
8. As a user, I want future voice, mobile, pager-like, or other capture surfaces to submit ideas without becoming mandatory dependencies, so that the workflow can adapt to how ideas actually occur.
9. As a user, I want multiple agents to execute ready work within explicit capacity and permission policies, so that a swarm increases throughput without becoming uncontrolled.
10. As a LouiseLM user, I want the project to ship one coherent example configuration of my current workflow, so that I can dogfood the system while other users compose different workflows.

## Implementation Decisions

- Treat capture, organization, deliberation, planning, execution, and observation as distinct workflow stages.
- Keep raw ideas local and user-owned by default; remote services are opt-in configuration.
- Use existing headless sessions and typed events as extension boundaries. Do not invent a formal plugin API or event schema before real slices require it.
- Make recommendations explainable and policy-controlled. Automated organization and resurfacing may be configurable; implementation remains approval-gated.
- Keep Neovim as LouiseLM’s deliberate home and operator cockpit while preserving headless automation.
- Use adapters for future capture surfaces rather than making mobile, voice, or a separate daemon part of the core requirement.
- Use the current grill-me → plan → to-beads → br/bv/bvr → coding-agent workflow as a first-party example configuration, not a hard dependency.
- Consider beads-style status/group/agent capacity policies when the swarm orchestrator reaches implementation; the related beads_rust capacity work is prior art, not a LouiseLM dependency.

## Testing Decisions

- Each vertical slice must test observable behavior through public APIs.
- Capture tests must prove that the active conversation continues and that the raw idea survives disposal, restart, or late background work.
- Resurfacing tests must cover the default session-end boundary and configurable event boundaries.
- Recommendation tests must assert stable reasons and preserve raw source data; policy tests must cover show, queue, grill, and approval-gated execution paths.
- Adapter and control-plane tests should use deterministic fakes and headless smoke coverage; no real devices, network services, or credentials.
- The example configuration must be runnable against the existing mock ACP agent and must not require br, bv, bvr, or a particular model to be installed for core tests.

## Out of Scope

- Making this epic ready for implementation now; it is intentionally deferred while the alpha ACP chat foundation is dogfooded.
- A general notes application or non-software outcome manager.
- A mandatory Android app, voice backend, pager device, hosted service, or editor-independent runtime.
- A formal LouiseLM plugin marketplace or extension API before concrete substitution points emerge.
- Choosing graph versus tree for the control-plane presentation before real usage provides evidence.
- Replacing CodeCompanion or judging its capabilities.

## Further Notes

This is a memory anchor for the ideas surfaced during product grilling, not a commitment to implement every slice at once. When one slice becomes worth pursuing, split it into a focused feature or task, attach only true dependencies, and leave the remaining epic deferred.

title: ACP session options and resource telemetry UX
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM can select an adapter only when the first chat is created, and it currently discards ACP session configuration options and usage/context updates. Users cannot change an agent-advertised model or reasoning setting after startup, cannot see which settings are active, and cannot tell whether a long autonomous session is approaching its context limit or waiting on a permission request. Starting multiple sessions also lacks explicit navigation and cleanup controls.

## Solution

Add a generic ACP session-controls and observability UX. After `session/new` becomes ready, open a token-free setup overview of all supported agent-advertised select and boolean options; allow idle-only changes through a public chat method and `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, refreshing the complete option list after each update. Add explicit `:LouiselmCancel`, `:LouiselmNewSession`, `:LouiselmSwitchSession`, and `:LouiselmCloseSession` commands. Keep existing sessions running when a new one starts, expose their state through compact headers and switcher rows, and dispose sessions explicitly when closed. Render passive context-pressure states, reported cumulative cost, active settings, lifecycle state, permission waiting, compaction/tool activity, and optional experimental per-turn usage fields without estimating tokens or prices.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to choose model and other ACP session options before my first prompt, so that each new session starts with deliberate settings.
2. As a user, I want to change supported options while a session is idle, so that future turns use the new configuration without restarting the session.
3. As a user, I want busy sessions to refuse option changes and offer explicit cancellation, so that autonomous turns are not reconfigured mid-flight.
4. As a user, I want to see active settings, lifecycle state, context pressure, cost, and reported usage, so that I can monitor long-running work.
5. As a user, I want to create, switch between, and close concurrent sessions, so that multiple adapters can work without leaking processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A ready new session with supported ACP config options opens an overview picker before the first prompt; Esc accepts agent defaults and an agent with no supported options skips the picker.
2. The overview renders every supported select/boolean option in agent order, supports selecting values, applies `session/set_config_option`, replaces the local list with the complete response, and handles agent-pushed `config_option_update` notifications.
3. Option changes are rejected while prompting, cancelling, or waiting for permission; `:LouiselmCancel` requests cancellation and late callbacks cannot revive disposed UI or sessions.
4. The client advertises boolean config-option support and ignores unknown future option types while rejecting malformed consumed fields.
5. `:LouiselmNewSession` chooses an adapter, creates a separate session, and opens its setup picker without cancelling existing sessions; `:LouiselmSwitchSession` selects attached sessions using compact agent/state/options/context/cost rows.
6. `:LouiselmCloseSession` confirms only for active or permission-blocked sessions, disposes the selected session/process, removes its chat buffer, and leaves other sessions running.
7. Session headers show exact lifecycle/activity state, all active options, context used/size/percentage with passive 75/90/95% warning states, stale context after model changes until refreshed, and reported cumulative cost when available.
8. Completed turns append a compact usage footer only for reported fields; optional experimental usage fields are validated defensively, never estimated or supplemented with adapter-specific fallbacks.
9. Compaction remains agent-owned: render generic ACP tool/compaction activity and context-meter changes, but add no LouiseLM manual compaction API in this phase.
10. Headless session snapshots/events expose typed configuration, lifecycle, permission, context, cost, and usage state for a future monitor; no swarm dashboard or orchestration is included.

## Implementation Notes

- Extend the session lifecycle and ACP validation at the shared boundary; preserve complete option-list replacement and asynchronous main-loop scheduling.
- Enrich `session:inspect()` and typed events rather than deriving telemetry from rendered buffers.
- Keep `LLM_MODEL` in the caller-owned schema/config example; do not add a universal built-in schema that rejects provider-specific environment variables.
- Preserve agent-provided defaults, session history, cumulative cost, and existing slash-command passthrough. Mark context telemetry stale after model changes until the agent reports a new effective window.

## Testing Notes

- Add focused mini.test coverage for option parsing, dependent option refresh, boolean capability advertisement, malformed/unknown options, idle-only transitions, cancellation, permission waiting, and disposal/late results.
- Add headless UI smoke tests for setup/overview flow, command behavior, headers, passive thresholds, usage footer omission, compaction/tool rendering, multiple-session navigation, and close confirmation.
- Exercise ACP notifications and process callbacks through scheduled production boundaries; use the mock ACP agent and no real credentials or agent binaries.

## Out of Scope

- Manual compaction or a hard-coded `:LouiselmCompact` command.
- A generic advertised-command picker.
- A swarm dashboard, orchestration, capacity policy, worktree isolation, or subagent aggregation.
- Adapter-specific usage parsers, pricing tables, tokenizers, or cache-cost estimates.
- A universal built-in configuration schema.
close_reason: Implemented ACP select/boolean session options, typed lifecycle/context/cost/usage state, setup and multi-session commands, safe scheduled UI updates, documentation, and passing StyLua/LuaLS/95-test gates

title: LouieLM chat crashes in vim.schedule callback
description:
## Problem

A LouieLM chat session reports a runtime error from a scheduled callback:

```text
vim.schedule callback: ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:370: 'repl
```

The error text was captured as truncated after `repl`; the full trailing message may need to be obtained from the Neovim message area or log.

## Expected behavior

Scheduled LouieLM UI callbacks should handle the session state safely and must not raise an error while rendering or updating the chat.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Reproduce and identify the operation at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:370` that produces the invalid `repl`-related value/error.
2. Fix the underlying error without breaking normal LouieLM chat updates.
3. Verify that model responses, tool/status updates, and scheduled UI rendering complete without an uncaught `vim.schedule callback` error.
4. Add or update a regression test where practical.

Source report: /tmp/nvim-uqo.md

title: Stack LouieLM transcript content in chronological order
description:
## Problem

In the latest screenshot of a LouieLM session, the transcript content feels split by type: the conversation text appears above while tool activity/status lines are grouped at the bottom near the prompt. This makes the sequence of the session awkward to follow.

## Desired behavior

Render each printed item in one chronological vertical stack, including model text, user text, tool calls, tool results, and status messages. New items should appear after the preceding item in the same transcript flow, with the composer/input area remaining at the bottom.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Model text, user text, tool activity, tool results, and status messages appear in a single chronological transcript order.
2. Tool output is positioned next to or directly after the event that produced it rather than in a separate bottom group.
3. The input/composer remains clearly separated from transcript history at the bottom.
4. Existing session header and chat behavior remain unchanged.

title: Show whose turn it is in LouieLM chat
description:
## Problem

During a LouieLM chat session, the top red header shows the session option, but it does not indicate whether the model is currently sending text or whether it is the user's turn to respond.

## Desired behavior

Add a visible status indicator in the chat header that distinguishes at least:

- Model is responding/sending text
- Your turn / waiting for user input

The indicator should update as the conversation state changes and remain consistent with the actual session state. Preserve the existing red session-option header.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A LouieLM chat session visibly shows whether the model is currently responding or it is the user's turn.
2. The status changes promptly when model output starts, finishes, or the session becomes ready for user input.
3. The indicator is understandable without relying on color alone (for example, include text or an icon with accessible labeling).
4. Existing session-option header behavior remains intact.

title: Investigate diff edit approval UX
description:
## Context

After asking LouiseLM to create a file, the plugin opened a `louiselm-diff` buffer. The latest screenshot (`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0457_1920x1200_1786244259.png`) shows the target path, `--- original`, `+++ proposed`, and an otherwise empty buffer. No visible accept/reject/close actions or instructions are presented, and Neovim is in insert mode.

## Investigation

Determine the intended lifecycle for an agent-proposed file edit and whether this diff view is currently incomplete, incorrectly rendered, or intentionally only a review surface. Trace the permission/edit/diff flow and document how a user should:

- understand what changed;
- accept/apply the proposed edit;
- reject it;
- cancel or return to the conversation;
- handle an empty/new-file diff;
- recover if the diff buffer is closed or the proposed edit becomes stale.

Assess the UX from a first-time user perspective, including discoverability of keymaps/commands, mode choice, statusline/help text, and whether approval belongs in the diff view, a permission prompt, or both.

## Exit criteria

- Reproduce the flow with a deterministic test or documented local scenario.
- Identify the root cause of the empty/unactionable presentation, if it is a bug.
- State the intended user-facing contract and recommended minimal UX changes.
- Add implementation follow-up beads tasks if the investigation finds separate fixes.
- Add or update headless UI behavior coverage for the confirmed contract where practical.
close_reason: Added discoverable diff approval instructions and normal-mode focus; verified full test and quality gates.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Investigation complete. The diff controller already had buffer-local normal-mode mappings: a accepts, d/q reject. The screenshot was unfriendly because the review buffer provided no instructions and inherited insert mode from the chat prompt, making those mappings undiscoverable/unusable. The diff is a permission review; accept sends the ACP allow response and the agent performs the write. Added an explicit instruction line and return to normal mode on focus. Existing behavior tests plus the new render assertion pass; no separate apply bug was reproduced.

title: Typing during active turn inserts red buffer error
description:
## Reproduction
1. Start a LouiseLM chat session.
2. While the model is responding / it is not the user's turn, type into the chat buffer.
3. Observe the buffer and Neovim message area.

## Observed
The chat buffer displays a red error/traceback while handling the typed input:
`vim.schedule callback: .../lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:145: replacement string item contains newlines`
The traceback points through `nvim_buf_set_lines`, `set_line`, and `handle_event`. The UI later appears normal once the turn completes (see second screenshot), but the transient error is user-visible and may indicate that streamed/event updates race with edits made while the session is active.

## Expected
Typing while it is not the user's turn should be safely rejected, queued, or otherwise handled without a red traceback or corrupted chat buffer. Any user-facing feedback should be intentional and clear.

## Evidence
- First screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0501_1920x1200_1786244489.png`
- Second screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0501_1920x1200_1786244505.png`

## Acceptance criteria
- Reproduce the issue deterministically with a mock/fast event sequence if possible.
- Identify whether the root cause is newline-containing content being passed as one `nvim_buf_set_lines` replacement item, a turn-state race, or both.
- Prevent the red traceback and preserve the intended chat content during active-turn typing.
- Add regression coverage for input arriving while streamed updates are being applied.
